equity.level_reason: Breastfeeding percentages are reported by mother's race/ethnicity and described as progress toward a common target, but no between-group disparity is framed or quantified; the 'nearly doubled' multiple is a within-group period change.

level_alternative.reason: Group values are judged against the Healthy People 2010 target of 75% 'in all racial/ethnic groups', which could be read as a quantified shortfall by race.

ev.q: Substantial progress toward meeting this goal has been observed among Hispanic (75%) and non-Hispanic white (69%) mothers.

notes: Figures come from a published NSFG 2002 report (Chandra et al. 2005); read as yes because the QuickStats makes its own period and group comparisons, but limited (cited figures) is defensible. Design inferred from the survey source; twins and higher-order births excluded.
view_issues: Figure values are not in the packet; only the text gives group percentages, and the 1990–1993 values for Hispanic and white mothers are not stated.
